meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'where'.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

находиться.gloss: to be located, to be found

meanings.en: to be located, to be situated
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ходиться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be located', forming an aspectual pair with 'найтись'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: Where is the operating room located?
The town is situated on a river.
Where is the operating room located here?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'again'.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: to pull or bring someone or something somewhere

examples.trans: He dragged the suitcase into the room.

examples.text: Ты опять затащил меня в постель?
examples.trans: Did you drag me into bed again?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: furniture or place prepared for sleeping

examples.text: Ты опять затащил меня в постель?
examples.trans: Did you drag me into bed again?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'of course'.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: to fasten together with cords or rope

examples.trans: He tied the rope with a strong knot.

examples.text: Конечно, связал и принёс сюда сам.
examples.trans: Of course, tied you up and brought you here myself.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
смеяться над кем = to laugh at someone; perfective засмеяться = to start laughing
Secondary conversational sense ('to laugh at') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Don't laugh. Read me the number.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'it is necessary'.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звонить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'звонить'.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: ночью = at night; спокойной ночи = good night

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'club', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('club, society') (спортивный клуб = sports club) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: In the evening we're going to a club.

examples.text: Ты у нас в клубе танцевала!
examples.trans: You used to dance at our club!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'nonsense'.
Secondary conversational sense ('stupidity, foolishness') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Что за глупости? Значит, Осипенко сам эти деньги украл!
examples.trans: What nonsense? That means Osipenko stole that money himself!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cry, to weep', paired with 'заплакать'.

examples.trans: Why is the little girl crying?

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'receiver'.
Secondary conversational sense ('tube, pipe') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Russian numeral ('three') that declines for case and governs case agreement on the counted noun.

examples.trans: We give him three days. That's it.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hour', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('o'clock') (в два часа = at two o'clock) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'll be there in an hour.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

час.governs: after 2, 3, 4 and полтора the genitive часа is stressed on the ending

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Secondary conversational sense ('to beg') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

забрать.gloss: to take back, to take away

meanings.en: to take away, to pick up
meanings.note: забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement
забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'home'.

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.

examples.text: Так, мы идём к слепым. А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

воспользоваться.gloss: to take advantage of, to use

meanings.en: to take advantage of, to use
meanings.note: to make use of an opportunity or situation

examples.trans: He took advantage of the moment.

examples.text: Ты просто воспользовался моей минутной слабостью.
examples.trans: You simply took advantage of my momentary weakness.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
lasting only a short time or moment

examples.text: Ты просто воспользовался моей минутной слабостью.
examples.trans: You simply took advantage of my momentary weakness.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'weakness'.

examples.trans: You're taking advantage of my weakness!

examples.text: Ты просто воспользовался моей минутной слабостью.
examples.trans: You simply took advantage of my momentary weakness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасти'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to save', forming an aspectual pair with 'спасать'.

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович, я на минуточку. Я спасла монастырь!
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich, I'll only be a minute. I saved the monastery!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'from' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('of') (тошнит от = sick of) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'trouble'.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

уйти.gloss: to leave, to go away (on foot)

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away (on foot)', paired with 'уходить'.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'from here'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: singular in Russian, unlike English

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.en: to lie, to be lying down, to rest
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to lie', forming an aspectual pair with 'полежать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Такие люди должны лежать в особенном месте!
examples.trans: Such people should lie in a special place!
The book is lying on the table.
But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('that') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'
Declinable masculine noun meaning 'chair', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Put the chair by the table.

examples.text: А зачем нам бревно? Я вот стулья взял!
examples.trans: And why do we need a log? I brought folding chairs right here!

meanings.note: needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Secondary conversational sense ('owe') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
